clue.text: Found in 8 after prohibition in India

indicators.note: after says the abundance word follows the prohibition word

parts.note: a prohibition is a ban
8 down is ABUNDANCE, and 'in abundance' means galore

explanation.surface: Something discovered in plenty once a ban was lifted somewhere in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 8' stands for 'in abundance', which is GALORE; 'Found' just joins it to the definition, a place in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore (Bengaluru) is a major city in southern India, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: English put in optimum form when threatened

indicators.note: put in tells us the English letter is placed inside the word for top form

parts.note: in optimum form means at your best

explanation.surface: An Englishman brings out his best when under threat.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beset is to be harassed or assailed on all sides, which is being threatened.

clue.text: Relation of a bishop in state

indicators.note: in places the article and the bishop inside the word for a state

parts.note: a nation is a state
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A family relative of a bishop living in some country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a family member but means the telling of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation can be an account or telling of events, which is a narration.

clue.text: Rate of one cheeky bash at a classic cuckold

parts.note: MPH, miles per hour, is a rate of speed
I is the Roman numeral one
a try-on is a cheeky attempt, a bash at something

explanation.surface: A cheeky go at speed by someone, aimed at a famous wronged husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'at' are links; the article A comes first. In Greek myth Amphitryon was cuckolded by Zeus, who took his form to lie with his wife Alcmene.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphitryon, husband of Alcmene, was deceived by Zeus, making him the classic cuckold of mythology.

clue.text: Possibly, a Roman's stroke?

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of a Roman's might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Perhaps a stroke of the pen or sword belonging to an ancient Roman?
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing the stroke is the oarsman sitting nearest the stern who sets the rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: The stroke is the rower who sets the pace for the crew, so a stroke is one particular rower.

clue.text: Initial duty with its administrators cut out

parts.note: Customs and Excise were the administrators of duty, so the Excise administers it

indicators.note: Initial picks just the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The first tax collected along with those who administer it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two parts; Excise (as in Customs and Excise) is the body that runs duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Excised means removed by cutting, so it is a synonym of cut out.

clue.text: Lady entertainer without qualification

indicators.note: without means the qualification is removed from the entertainer's name

parts.note: Madonna is the pop singer and entertainer
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree qualification

explanation.surface: A female performer with no formal training.
explanation.definitionFit: Donna is the Italian word and title for a lady.

clue.text: What's cast by model that she has to watch?

definitions.text: What's cast by model that she has to watch?

parts.note: a die is what is cast in a dice game
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: What a fashion model must keep an eye on, cast by the model herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' joins the parts; the whole clue also describes the eating plan a model monitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Models famously watch their food intake, so this is what a model has to watch.

clue.text: Is it green to take up bottled water?

indicators.note: in a down answer, take up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Evian is a well-known brand of bottled water

explanation.surface: Is it environmentally friendly to drink bottled water?
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests ecology but means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the sense of inexperienced or innocent means naive.

clue.text: A cakewalk is more than enough

parts.note: a cakewalk is a dance, read here as a cake (bun) plus a dance

explanation.surface: Something easy is more than you need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cakewalk' usually means an easy task; here it splits into cake (BUN) and the dance it really is (DANCE).
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is a plentiful supply, more than enough of something.

clue.text: Such as Paul getting blame and punishment

parts.note: Paul is a saint, abbreviated ST
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: Someone like Paul being blamed and punished.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap was a leather belt used for beating, and the strap means corporal punishment.

clue.text: French statesman took his place with wealthy English

parts.note: rich means wealthy
in lieu means in place of, so lieu is a place taken

explanation.surface: A French politician stepped into the shoes of a rich Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Richelieu was chief minister to Louis XIII of France, a famous statesman.

clue.text: Could great music be 1 of 9?

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of great music may become something else

explanation.surface: Could a great piece of music be one of nine?
explanation.walkthrough: '1 of 9' is not a cross-reference: there are nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Melpomene, the Muse of tragedy, is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth.

clue.text: Flex, though copper is the more likely material

definitions.meaning: a flex is an electric cable
the soft heavy metal is a material

explanation.surface: An electric cable, though copper would be the more likely stuff for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: a flex is a lead, yet you would expect it to be made of copper, not the metal of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead is a flex in British usage, and lead the metal is a material.

clue.text: Summer breakdown? Call out RAC

indicators.note: a breakdown means the letters of the following words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist has broken down and phones the RAC, the British motoring rescue service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is not the season but one who sums. The RAC is a British breakdown service.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer is a thing that adds up figures, which a calculator does.

clue.text: Letter from funny man losing head — 19 down girl's suitor …

indicators.note: losing head drops the first letter of the comedian word

parts.note: a comic is a funny man
19 down's girl is Eth of the Glums, whose suitor was Ron

explanation.surface: A note from a comedian who has lost his head over a girl's boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glums was a British radio comedy sketch in which Ron was engaged to Eth.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Start to hold forth over a single shot of the hard stuff

indicators.note: to hold means the speechifying word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: to hold forth is to orate, speak at length
I, the Roman numeral one, is a single
gin is a spirit, the hard stuff

explanation.surface: Someone starts holding forth after one shot of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' and 'over' are links; 'hold forth' looks like one phrase but 'to hold' is the container and 'forth' gives ORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or bring into being, a synonym of start.

clue.text: … with expression of late Piper

parts.note: late means dead
the god Pan played the pipes

explanation.surface: Continuing: with the look of a departed piper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'of' are links; the ellipsis carries on from the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan is an expressionless face, a deliberately blank expression.

clue.text: Advertising concert with no one to turn up

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert

indicators.note: in a down answer turn up reads the words from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A concert with nobody turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses NO + I + TO into OTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is the publicising of a product, which is advertising.

clue.text: Like fire in turn goes off

indicators.note: off means the letters go wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: a U-turn, so turn gives U

explanation.surface: Like a fire that goes out in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous means relating to or resembling fire.

clue.text: Boy raised hand entirely for his own indulgence

indicators.note: in a down answer raised reads the boy's name upwards

parts.note: Les is a boy's name
a fist is the whole hand clenched

explanation.surface: A lad puts up his whole hand for his own pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses LES into SEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfist is someone who acts for his own gratification.

clue.text: Space many forfeit when shut in

parts.note: an en is a printing space
C, Roman 100, stands for many
to forfeit is to lose

explanation.surface: Many give up space when locked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose something is to shut it in.

clue.text: Glum girl has to take out loan for fuel

parts.note: Eth was the girl in the Glums radio comedy

indicators.note: take out suggests the loan letters are taken apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy girl needs a loan to buy petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glums was a British radio comedy; Eth was Ron's fiancée.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol is alcohol used as a fuel.

clue.text: One past villain

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Somebody once a bad man.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the villain of Othello.

clue.text: One wears a decoration on the way out

indicators.note: wears means the decoration goes around the one

parts.note: gong is slang for a medal or decoration
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sports a medal as he leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Going means leaving, on the way out.

clue.text: The lot — how's about that? November starts here

parts.note: the lot means all

indicators.note: about means the word goes around

parts.note: how's written without its apostrophe
that refers back to the lot, all

explanation.surface: Everything, how about that? The month begins now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' does not link: it stands for the lot again, so the same three letters go both first and inside the abbreviated 'how's'.
explanation.definitionFit: All Hallows, All Saints' Day, falls on 1 November, so the month starts with it.

clue.text: Drama viewed by audience

indicators.note: by audience means as heard by listeners

parts.note: viewed means seen

explanation.surface: A play watched by spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a drama or fuss, as in to make a scene.

clue.text: Peter's in no peril

definitions.meaning: peter is criminal slang for a ..., the 's standing for is

explanation.walkthrough: Peter is old thieves' slang for a strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A peter is slang for a strongbox; free from danger also means secure.

clue.text: Technique pioneered by Disney into a main production

indicators.note: production means the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A method Disney pioneered goes into a major production.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney pioneered cartoon animation, making drawings appear to move.

clue.text: Instant cereal from the heart of Patna

indicators.note: the heart of picks the middle letter of the word

parts.note: rice is a cereal

explanation.surface: Quick-cooking rice from the centre of Patna, a city in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Patna rice is a long-grain rice named after the Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in a trice' means in a moment, so a trice is a very short instant of time.

clue.text: Zealous speech could be a bore

indicators.note: speech means as spoken out

parts.note: zealous means eager

explanation.surface: Enthusiastic chatter might be tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull person but is a tidal wave in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagre is a tidal bore, a wave rushing up a river.

clue.text: Virtue the church has first to learn with difficulty

indicators.note: has first means the other piece comes before the church
with difficulty suggests the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A virtue the church must learn with difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance, patient acceptance of differing views or behaviour, is regarded as a moral virtue.
